chapter_title_en: Stirrings Beyond the Seas; Claiming the Treasure
chapter_seo_title: Treasure Light Pavilion: Han Li’s Calculated Looting Strategy | RMJI Chapter 476
chapter_meta_description: Han Li enters the Treasure Light Pavilion! After dismissing first-floor junk treasures, he uses his Gold Devourer Beetles to crack a self-healing barrier on the second floor and pits three ancient treasures against each other.
og_title: A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality Ch. 476 - The Vault of Treasures
og_description: Han Li bypasses cheap replicas and high-tier barriers alike with methodical logic and a swarm of beetles—what will he choose for his next ace in the hole?
twitter_description: Han Li finds an ancient treasure vault, ignores the common picks, and breaks into the top-tier stockpile using his bug swarm. Classic systematic looting in action.

lore_anchors.definition: The protected vault within the ancient pocket dimension of this arc, holding sealed ancient treasures arranged across two floors with escalating security.
Magical tools from the primordial era; often less refined than modern magic tools in pure power, but prized for unique, rare abilities that have no modern equivalent.
A swarm of spirit insects domesticated by Han Li; capable of devouring metal, spiritual energy barriers, and other hardened defenses at a consistent, relentless rate.
A display stand made from spirit jade, used in ancient vaults to house and seal individual treasures with a semi-circular light barrier.
A property of certain restricted zones or formations that prevents a cultivator from projecting their spiritual perception, forcing them to rely on physical senses.
An ancient treasure composed of five linked rings, each corresponding to one of the Five Elements (Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water); suggests an ability that draws on or balances elemental forces.
A mirror-type ancient treasure; in xianxia, mirror artifacts are consistently depicted as possessing rare or unpredictable spatial, reflective, or illusion-based powers.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn’t Han Li just grab multiple treasures from the second floor?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The barrier’s self-healing was too fast; he only had a single opening created by his beetles and managed to slip in for one pick before it closed entirely.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li dismiss the first-floor treasures?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He already owns a high-power flying sword formation (Azure Bamboo Cloudswarm Swords); the first-floor halberds and lances are no better than common magic tools and offer no upgrade.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What’s the significance of Han Li’s final three picks?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The mirror is a classic “wild card” artifact; the five rings suggest multi-elemental control (rare and powerful); and the dark-red cloak likely provides concealment or defense—perfect for Han Li’s survival-oriented style.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can’t Han Li use his divine sense inside the light barrier?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The barrier’s suppression effect is an intended security feature: it prevents cultivators from scanning the treasures’ power, forcing them to gamble on intuition rather than data.
